- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment volatility is high (frequent +1.00/-1.00 swings) and news volume is elevated, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–4% to avoid noise amplification.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If true outcome consistently exceeds model by 2–5% over 30d, model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 10–15 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.
- If news volume is high (≥3.0) and sentiment is mixed, model overfits to short-term noise; reduce forecast volatility by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
